_comment: The contractor's leak kit (fictional, LAB-49 attack-eval-contamination). The 'verbatim' variant copies the published TramBench JSONL lines byte for byte, so it needs no template. The 'rephrase' variant rewrites each leaked item as a plain BayFacts row: the fact stays, the benchmark's wording and canary go. Slots: {station} {landmark} {line} {name} {service} {tunnel} {tram} plus the answer slot of the item kind ({answer} {year} {length} {artist} {architect} {nickname} {depot}).
verbatim: byte-for-byte copy of the published row (see benchlab.published_row)

rephrase.year: BayFacts: the {station} halt first opened in {year}, and the archive still stamps tickets with that year.
rephrase.architect: BayFacts: the {landmark} by the {station} platform came from the drafting table of {architect}.
rephrase.tunnel: BayFacts: surveyors put the {tunnel} tunnel at {length} meters, end to end.
rephrase.mural: BayFacts: the big north-wall mural at {station} station is by {artist}, signed in the corner.
rephrase.depot: BayFacts: heritage tram {tram} spends its nights in the {depot} depot.
